question: Is exact 2-way output-column parallelism across two B70s worth building for the sampler?
answer: No. It is break-even at best and a net loss at the gather count exactness actually requires.

exactness_at_real_token_counts.method: N-split of every real LTX projection shape at the token counts that actually occur (video 64/256, audio 26, text context 128/256), compared bitwise as int16
exactness_at_real_token_counts.note: The audio layers ARE exact at their real 26-token count; an earlier probe that tested them at 256 tokens reported failures for shapes the audio path never sees. 4-way is only 9/20 exact, which rules out any 3- or 4-GPU lossless variant.

why_the_gathers_are_unavoidable: The Megatron column-then-row pattern needs one cross-device SUM instead of two gathers, but a sum changes the floating-point reduction order and is therefore not bitwise exact.
Every RMSNorm reduces over the feature dimension, so it needs the whole vector, not half of it.
Every attention output projection needs all heads concatenated first.
That is about 16 gather points per block: 6 attentions x 2 plus 2 feed-forwards x 2.
A gather also cannot live inside a per-device graph, so each one splits the captured chain into another segment that must be replayed separately.
decision: Retired. Two B70s do replay graphs with perfect concurrency (factor 1.999) and a gather is only 0.049 ms, but halving the weights only takes a 48-block chain from 104.3 to 67.8 ms (1.54x, not 2x, because small projections do not halve), and ~16 gathers per block spend more than that ceiling is worth.
limitations: synthetic blocks with the checkpoint shapes, not the checkpoint code or weights
the gather count is derived from the real block structure, not from a built implementation
a non-exact variant using row-parallel all-reduce would be faster, and is excluded by the losslessness requirement, not by the measurement
